You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

content.content:
1	// CRDT state sits beside the change log as an independent, automatically
2	// mergeable state layer. A document's CRDT type is declared with its first
3	// operation batch — "counter", "gset" (a grow-only set) or "register" (a
4	// last-writer-wins register) — and never changes afterward; two batches
5	// declaring different types concurrently serialize in one transaction and
6	// exactly one takes effect.
7	//
8	// A counter operation carries the originating device's accumulated
9	// contribution. Each device's contribution only moves forward (a regressing
10	// value is an ErrCRDTConflict and changes nothing), and the merged state is the
11	// sum of every device's maximum contribution — a PN-free grow-only counter
12	// (GCounter), so the merge is commutative, associative and idempotent.
13	//
14	// A gset operation adds elements; the merged state is the union of every
15	// accepted element, presented in ascending order. Re-adding an element does
16	// not change the state.
17	//
18	// A register operation carries an arbitrary JSON value (null, number, string,
19	// array or object, stored verbatim) and a non-negative integer version. A
20	// device's versions only move strictly forward (a regressing or equal version
21	// is an ErrCRDTConflict and changes nothing), and the merged state is the
22	// value of the operation with the greatest version, ties broken by the
23	// lexicographically smaller operation id — a last-writer-wins register whose
24	// merge is commutative, associative and idempotent, so every reader converges
25	// to the same value regardless of arrival order.
26	//
27	// Every operation carries a stable, client-supplied id, unique per document.
28	// Re-posting the same id with the same content and origin is idempotent; the
29	// same id with different content or a different device is an
30	// ErrCRDTConflict and leaves the state untouched. Operations and the merged
31	// result commit together in one serialized transaction and are durable: the
32	// decisions and the merged state are unchanged after a restart.
33	//
34	// The CRDT layer shares the registration/permission layer with the rest of the
35	// service: an unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and a revoked
36	// device yields ErrPermissionDenied (403), before any CRDT content is observed.
37	// It never touches the change log, document cursors, snapshots or the
38	// subscription machinery.
39	
40	package store
41	
42	import (
43		"database/sql"
44		"encoding/json"
45		"errors"
46		"fmt"
47	)
48	
49	// CRDT document types.
50	const (
51		// CRDTTypeCounter is the grow-only counter: the merged value is the sum of
52		// each device's maximum accumulated contribution.
53		CRDTTypeCounter = "counter"
54		// CRDTTypeGSet is the grow-only set: the merged value is the union of all
55		// added elements.
56		CRDTTypeGSet = "gset"
57		// CRDTTypeRegister is the last-writer-wins register: the merged value is
58		// the value of the operation with the greatest version, ties broken by the
59		// lexicographically smaller operation id.
60		CRDTTypeRegister = "register"
61	)
62	
63	// ErrCRDTNotFound reports that no CRDT operation has ever been committed for
64	// the document, so it has neither a type nor a merged state yet. The caller
65	// maps it to 404.
66	var ErrCRDTNotFound = errors.New("crdt state not found")
67	
68	// ErrCRDTConflict reports a rejected CRDT batch: the document's type is
69	// already fixed to another type, a counter contribution regressed, or an
70	// operation id already exists with different content or origin. Nothing is
71	// written; the caller maps it to 409.
72	type ErrCRDTConflict struct {
73		// ID is the conflicting operation id when one is known; it is empty for a
74		// document-level conflict (a mismatched declared type).
75		ID string
76		// Reason carries a short, machine-facing description of the conflict.
77		Reason string
78	}
79	
80	func (e *ErrCRDTConflict) Error() string {
81		if e.ID != "" {
82			return fmt.Sprintf("crdt conflict for operation %q: %s", e.ID, e.Reason)
83		}
84		return "crdt conflict: " + e.Reason
85	}
86	
87	// CRDTOp is one element of an inbound CRDT batch.
88	//
89	// For a counter, Value is the device's accumulated contribution: it must be a
90	// JSON number that is a non-negative integer, and it may never decrease for
91	// the same device. Elements and Version are unused.
92	//
93	// For a gset, Elements lists the strings the operation adds to the set and
94	// must be non-empty; Value and Version are unused.
95	//
96	// For a register, Value is an arbitrary JSON value stored verbatim and
97	// Version is a non-negative integer that must be strictly greater than every
98	// version the same device has already had accepted. Elements is unused.
99	type CRDTOp struct {
100		ID       string          // client-supplied stable id, unique per document
101		DeviceID string          // originating device (shared by the whole batch)
102		Value    json.RawMessage // counter: accumulated contribution; register: the value
103		Elements []string        // gset: elements to add
104		Version  int64           // register: logical version, per-device strictly increasing
105	}
106	
107	// CRDTState is a document's merged CRDT state.
108	//
109	// Value holds the type-specific merged result: for a counter it decodes to the
110	// JSON integer sum of per-device maxima; for a gset it decodes to the sorted
111	// JSON array of every accepted element (an empty set is []); for a register it
112	// is the winning operation's JSON value, exactly as submitted.
113	type CRDTState struct {
114		Type  string          `json:"type"`
115		Value json.RawMessage `json:"value"`
116	}
117	
118	// CRDTResult reports the outcome for one element of an accepted CRDT batch.
119	type CRDTResult struct {
120		ID      string `json:"id"`
121		Created bool   `json:"created"`
122	}
123	
124	// crdtSchema is appended to the schema created in init.
125	const crdtSchema = `
126	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_documents (
127		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
128		type        TEXT NOT NULL
129	);
130	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_ops (
131		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
132		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
133		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
134		value       BLOB,
135		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
136	);
137	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_counter_values (
138		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
139		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
140		value       INTEGER NOT NULL,
141		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
142	);
143	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_set_elements (
144		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
145		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
146		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element)
147	);
148	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_register_ops (
149		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
150		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
151		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
152		version     INTEGER NOT NULL,
153		value       BLOB NOT NULL,
154		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
155	);
156	`
157	
158	// SubmitCRDTOps validates and commits one CRDT batch atomically.
159	//
160	// declaredType is the type the client asserts for the document
161	// ("counter", "gset" or "register"). It fixes the type on the document's
162	// first batch; every later batch must declare the same type. Two batches
163	// declaring different types race in one serialized transaction, so exactly
164	// one wins and the other gets an *ErrCRDTConflict (409).
165	//
166	// The device is gated first (ErrDeviceNotFound / ErrPermissionDenied) before
167	// any CRDT content is read. Every operation is then resolved against the
168	// committed history: a repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and
169	// content, otherwise it is an *ErrCRDTConflict; a counter contribution below
170	// the device's current maximum, or a register version not strictly greater
171	// than the device's accepted versions, is likewise an *ErrCRDTConflict. Any
172	// failure rejects the whole batch. Results come back in request order.
173	//
174	// When the committed batch actually moved the merged state (a counter maximum
175	// advanced, the set union grew or the register's winning value changed) the
176	// document's CRDT state subscribers are notified with the new merged state
177	// after the commit; idempotent repeats, rejected batches and no-op additions
178	// change nothing and notify nobody.
179	func (s *Store) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []CRDTOp) ([]CRDTResult, error) {
180		// Serialize submissions with each other and with a subscriber's atomic
181		// register+initial-read: notifications then leave in commit order, and a
182		// committed state lands either in the initial read or in the queue.
183		s.crdtMu.Lock()
184		defer s.crdtMu.Unlock()
185	
186		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
187		if err != nil {
188			return nil, err
189		}
190		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
191	
192		deviceID := ops[0].DeviceID
193	
194		// Registration and permission are enforced before any CRDT content is
195		// observed, so a rejected submission cannot reveal type or state.
196		var deviceExists bool
197		if err := tx.QueryRow(
198			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
199		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
200			return nil, err
201		}
202		if !deviceExists {
203			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
204		}
205		var storedAuth int
206		err = tx.QueryRow(
207			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
208			documentID, deviceID,
209		).Scan(&storedAuth)
210		switch {
211		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
212			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
213		case err != nil:
214			return nil, err
215		default:
216			if storedAuth == 0 {
217				return nil, ErrPermissionDenied
218			}
219		}
220	
221		// Resolve the document type: fixed on the first accepted batch.
222		var docType string
223		err = tx.QueryRow(
224			`SELECT type FROM crdt_documents WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
225		).Scan(&docType)
226		switch {
227		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
228			// First batch for this document: its declared type wins the race.
229			if _, err := tx.Exec(
230				`INSERT INTO crdt_documents (document_id, type) VALUES (?, ?)`,
231				documentID, declaredType,
232			); err != nil {
233				return nil, err
234			}
235			docType = declaredType
236		case err != nil:
237			return nil, err
238		default:
239			if docType != declaredType {
240				return nil, &ErrCRDTConflict{
241					Reason: fmt.Sprintf("document type is already %q", docType),
242				}
243			}
244		}
245	
246		results := make([]CRDTResult, len(ops))
247	
248		var stateChanged bool
249		switch docType {
250		case CRDTTypeCounter:
251			changed, err := applyCounterOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
252			if err != nil {
253				return nil, err
254			}
255			stateChanged = changed
256		case CRDTTypeGSet:
257			changed, err := applyGSetOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
258			if err != nil {
259				return nil, err
260			}
261			stateChanged = changed
262		case CRDTTypeRegister:
263			changed, err := applyRegisterOps(tx, documentID, ops, results)
264			if err != nil {
265				return nil, err
266			}
267			stateChanged = changed
268		}
269	
270		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
271			return nil, err
272		}
273		if stateChanged {
274			// The committed batch moved the merged state; re-derive it (the merge
275			// is never cached) and publish it after commit, so a subscriber only
276			// ever observes a durable state and commits arrive in commit order.
277			state, err := s.GetCRDTState(documentID)
278			if err != nil {
279				return results, nil
280			}
281			s.notifyCRDTSubscribers(documentID, state)
282		}
283		return results, nil
284	}
285	
286	// applyCounterOps resolves and applies every counter operation inside tx. A
287	// repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and contribution. A new
288	// id with a contribution below the device's stored maximum regresses the
289	// counter and is rejected; an equal contribution is an accepted no-op; a
290	// larger one advances the device's maximum. It reports whether the merged
291	// state actually changed — only an advancing contribution moves the sum.
292	func applyCounterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
293		changed := false
294		for i, op := range ops {
295			value, err := decodeCounterValue(op.Value)
296			if err != nil {
297				return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: err.Error()}
298			}
299	
300			var existingDevice string
301			var existingValue []byte
302			err = tx.QueryRow(
303				`SELECT device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
304				documentID, op.ID,
305			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingValue)
306			switch {
307			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
308				// New id: enforce monotonicity against this device's maximum.
309				var current sql.NullInt64
310				if scanErr := tx.QueryRow(
311					`SELECT value FROM crdt_counter_values WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
312					documentID, op.DeviceID,
313				).Scan(&current); scanErr != nil && !errors.Is(scanErr, sql.ErrNoRows) {
314					return false, scanErr
315				}
316				if current.Valid && value < current.Int64 {
317					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
318						ID:     op.ID,
319						Reason: "counter contribution must not decrease",
320					}
321				}
322				if _, err := tx.Exec(
323					`INSERT INTO crdt_ops (document_id, id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
324					documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, []byte(op.Value),
325				); err != nil {
326					return false, err
327				}
328				if !current.Valid || value > current.Int64 {
329					if _, err := tx.Exec(
330						`INSERT INTO crdt_counter_values (document_id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
331						 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value`,
332						documentID, op.DeviceID, value,
333					); err != nil {
334						return false, err
335					}
336					changed = true
337				}
338				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
339			case err != nil:
340				return false, err
341			default:
342				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingValue, op.Value) {
343					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
344						ID:     op.ID,
345						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device or value",
346					}
347				}
348				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
349			}
350		}
351		return changed, nil
352	}
353	
354	// applyGSetOps resolves and applies every grow-only-set operation inside tx.
355	// A repeated id is idempotent only with the same device and the same set of
356	// elements (element order is irrelevant to the merge). New elements are
357	// inserted into the union table; re-adding an element changes nothing. It
358	// reports whether the merged state actually changed — only an element that
359	// was not already in the union moves it.
360	func applyGSetOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
361		changed := false
362		for i, op := range ops {
363			var existingDevice string
364			var existingElements []byte
365			err := tx.QueryRow(
366				`SELECT device_id, value FROM crdt_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
367				documentID, op.ID,
368			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingElements)
369			switch {
370			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
371				// New id; insert the op and its elements below.
372			case err != nil:
373				return false, err
374			default:
375				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || !stringSetEqual(existingElements, op.Elements) {
376					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
377						ID:     op.ID,
378						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device or elements",
379					}
380				}
381				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
382				continue
383			}
384	
385			if _, err := tx.Exec(
386				`INSERT INTO crdt_ops (document_id, id, device_id, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)`,
387				documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, []byte(encodeSetElements(op.Elements)),
388			); err != nil {
389				return false, err
390			}
391			for _, element := range op.Elements {
392				// The union table is an identity insert: a repeated element simply
393				// exists once, and only a genuinely new element moves the merge.
394				res, err := tx.Exec(
395					`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO crdt_set_elements (document_id, element) VALUES (?, ?)`,
396					documentID, element,
397				)
398				if err != nil {
399					return false, err
400				}
401				if n, err := res.RowsAffected(); err == nil && n > 0 {
402					changed = true
403				}
404			}
405			results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
406		}
407		return changed, nil
408	}
409	
410	// applyRegisterOps resolves and applies every register operation inside tx. A
411	// repeated id is idempotent only with the same device, version and value. A
412	// new id whose version is not strictly greater than every version already
413	// accepted from the same device regresses (or stalls) the device's clock and
414	// is rejected. It reports whether the merged state actually changed — only a
415	// change of the winning operation's value moves it.
416	func applyRegisterOps(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, ops []CRDTOp, results []CRDTResult) (bool, error) {
417		// The merged value before the batch, so a batch that leaves the winner's
418		// value untouched (an idempotent replay, or a new op that loses the
419		// last-writer-wins comparison) reports no change and notifies nobody.
420		prev, prevOK, err := registerWinner(tx, documentID)
421		if err != nil {
422			return false, err
423		}
424	
425		for i, op := range ops {
426			if op.Version < 0 {
427				// The API boundary rejects negative versions; a negative version
428				// here means the caller skipped validation.
429				return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{ID: op.ID, Reason: "register version must be a non-negative integer"}
430			}
431	
432			var existingDevice string
433			var existingVersion int64
434			var existingValue []byte
435			err := tx.QueryRow(
436				`SELECT device_id, version, value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
437				documentID, op.ID,
438			).Scan(&existingDevice, &existingVersion, &existingValue)
439			switch {
440			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
441				// New id: the device's versions only move strictly forward. The
442				// per-device maximum is derived from the accepted ops, so the
443				// decision is durable across restarts without extra state.
444				var maxVersion sql.NullInt64
445				if scanErr := tx.QueryRow(
446					`SELECT MAX(version) FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
447					documentID, op.DeviceID,
448				).Scan(&maxVersion); scanErr != nil {
449					return false, scanErr
450				}
451				if maxVersion.Valid && op.Version <= maxVersion.Int64 {
452					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
453						ID:     op.ID,
454						Reason: "register version must be greater than the device's previously accepted version",
455					}
456				}
457				if _, err := tx.Exec(
458					`INSERT INTO crdt_register_ops (document_id, id, device_id, version, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
459					documentID, op.ID, op.DeviceID, op.Version, []byte(op.Value),
460				); err != nil {
461					return false, err
462				}
463				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: true}
464			case err != nil:
465				return false, err
466			default:
467				if existingDevice != op.DeviceID || existingVersion != op.Version || !jsonEqual(existingValue, op.Value) {
468					return false, &ErrCRDTConflict{
469						ID:     op.ID,
470						Reason: "operation id already exists with a different device, version or value",
471					}
472				}
473				results[i] = CRDTResult{ID: op.ID, Created: false}
474			}
475		}
476	
477		next, nextOK, err := registerWinner(tx, documentID)
478		if err != nil {
479			return false, err
480		}
481		// The merge is the winner's value; a new winner carrying a JSON-equal
482		// value does not move the state.
483		changed := prevOK != nextOK || (prevOK && nextOK && !jsonEqual(prev, next))
484		return changed, nil
485	}
486	
487	// registerWinner returns the value the register currently merges to: the
488	// value of the accepted operation with the greatest version, ties broken by
489	// the lexicographically smaller operation id. It reports false when the
490	// document has no accepted register operation yet.
491	func registerWinner(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (json.RawMessage, bool, error) {
492		var value []byte
493		err := tx.QueryRow(
494			`SELECT value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ?
495			 ORDER BY version DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1`,
496			documentID,
497		).Scan(&value)
498		switch {
499		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
500			return nil, false, nil
501		case err != nil:
502			return nil, false, err
503		default:
504			return json.RawMessage(value), true, nil
505		}
506	}
507	
508	// decodeCounterValue requires raw to be a non-negative JSON integer with no
509	// fraction or exponent. Floats, strings, booleans and null are rejected at the
510	// API boundary; a malformed integer here means the caller skipped validation.
511	func decodeCounterValue(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, error) {
512		var n int64
513		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
514			return 0, errors.New("counter value must be a non-negative integer")
515		}
516		return n, nil
517	}
518	
519	// encodeSetElements renders the elements of one gset operation as a JSON array
520	// for durable storage of the original operation content.
521	func encodeSetElements(elements []string) json.RawMessage {
522		raw, err := json.Marshal(elements)
523		if err != nil {
524			// Strings always marshal.
525			return json.RawMessage("[]")
526		}
527		return raw
528	}
529	
530	// stringSetEqual reports whether raw (a JSON array of strings stored for a
531	// prior gset operation) contains exactly the elements of want, ignoring
532	// duplicates and order: the content of a set operation is the set of elements.
533	func stringSetEqual(raw json.RawMessage, want []string) bool {
534		var got []string
535		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &got); err != nil {
536			return false
537		}
538		set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(got))
539		for _, e := range got {
540			set[e] = struct{}{}
541		}
542		for _, e := range want {
543			if _, ok := set[e]; !ok {
544				return false
545			}
546			delete(set, e)
547		}
548		return len(set) == 0
549	}
550	
551	// GetCRDTState returns the merged CRDT state for documentID. A document with
552	// no committed operations yields ErrCRDTNotFound (the caller answers 404).
553	//
554	// The merged value is derived from the per-device maxima (counter), the union
555	// table (gset) or the version/id ordering of the accepted operations
556	// (register), not cached: it is exactly what any equivalent batch order would
557	// converge to.
558	func (s *Store) GetCRDTState(documentID string) (CRDTState, error) {
559		var docType string
560		err := s.db.QueryRow(
561			`SELECT type FROM crdt_documents WHERE document_id = ?`, documentID,
562		).Scan(&docType)
563		switch {
564		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
565			return CRDTState{}, ErrCRDTNotFound
566		case err != nil:
567			return CRDTState{}, err
568		}
569	
570		switch docType {
571		case CRDTTypeCounter:
572			var total int64
573			if err := s.db.QueryRow(
574				`SELECT COALESCE(SUM(value), 0) FROM crdt_counter_values WHERE document_id = ?`,
575				documentID,
576			).Scan(&total); err != nil {
577				return CRDTState{}, err
578			}
579			raw, err := json.Marshal(total)
580			if err != nil {
581				return CRDTState{}, err
582			}
583			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: raw}, nil
584		case CRDTTypeGSet:
585			rows, err := s.db.Query(
586				`SELECT element FROM crdt_set_elements WHERE document_id = ? ORDER BY element ASC`,
587				documentID,
588			)
589			if err != nil {
590				return CRDTState{}, err
591			}
592			elements := make([]string, 0)
593			for rows.Next() {
594				var element string
595				if err := rows.Scan(&element); err != nil {
596					_ = rows.Close()
597					return CRDTState{}, err
598				}
599				elements = append(elements, element)
600			}
601			if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
602				_ = rows.Close()
603				return CRDTState{}, err
604			}
605			_ = rows.Close()
606			raw, err := json.Marshal(elements)
607			if err != nil {
608				return CRDTState{}, err
609			}
610			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: raw}, nil
611		case CRDTTypeRegister:
612			// A document's type row commits together with its first batch, so a
613			// register document always has at least one accepted operation.
614			var value []byte
615			if err := s.db.QueryRow(
616				`SELECT value FROM crdt_register_ops WHERE document_id = ?
617				 ORDER BY version DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1`,
618				documentID,
619			).Scan(&value); err != nil {
620				return CRDTState{}, err
621			}
622			return CRDTState{Type: docType, Value: json.RawMessage(value)}, nil
623		default:
624			return CRDTState{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown crdt type %q stored for document", docType)
625		}
626	}

1	package server
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"net/http"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
10	)
11	
12	// crdtOpIn is one element of a CRDT submission. Exactly one content shape is
13	// meaningful depending on the declared document type: value for a counter,
14	// elements for a grow-only set, value plus version for a register.
15	type crdtOpIn struct {
16		ID       string          `json:"id"`
17		Value    json.RawMessage `json:"value"`
18		Elements []string        `json:"elements"`
19		Version  json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
20	}
21	
22	// crdtOpsRequest is the body of POST .../crdt/ops.
23	type crdtOpsRequest struct {
24		DeviceID string     `json:"deviceId"`
25		Type     string     `json:"type"`
26		Ops      []crdtOpIn `json:"ops"`
27	}
28	
29	// handleCRDTOps accepts a batch of CRDT operations for a document.
30	//
31	// The batch declares the document's type; the first accepted batch fixes it
32	// to counter, gset or register and every later batch must declare the same
33	// type. Two batches racing to declare different types serialize in one
34	// transaction: exactly one takes effect and the other is a 409 that writes
35	// nothing.
36	//
37	// The strict body contract matches the other JSON endpoints: application/json,
38	// one JSON value, no trailing content, a non-empty deviceId, a valid type, a
39	// non-empty ops array of elements with non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicate
40	// ids, and type-correct content (counter: an integer value; gset: an elements
41	// array; register: any JSON value — null included — plus a non-negative
42	// integer version). Any violation is a 400 with zero writes.
43	func handleCRDTOps(s *store.Store, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
44		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
45	
46		var req crdtOpsRequest
47		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
48			return
49		}
50		if req.DeviceID == "" {
51			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
52			return
53		}
54		if req.Type != store.CRDTTypeCounter && req.Type != store.CRDTTypeGSet && req.Type != store.CRDTTypeRegister {
55			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `type must be "counter", "gset" or "register"`)
56			return
57		}
58		if len(req.Ops) == 0 {
59			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "ops must be a non-empty array")
60			return
61		}
62	
63		ops := make([]store.CRDTOp, len(req.Ops))
64		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Ops))
65		for i, op := range req.Ops {
66			if op.ID == "" {
67				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each op must have a non-empty string id")
68				return
69			}
70			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
71				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate op id within batch: "+op.ID)
72				return
73			}
74			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
75	
76			crdtOp := store.CRDTOp{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID}
77			switch req.Type {
78			case store.CRDTTypeCounter:
79				v, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(op.Value)
80				if !ok {
81					writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each counter op must carry an integer value >= 0")
82					return
83				}
84				// Re-marshal the canonical integer so idempotency compares the
85				// decoded value rather than the client's literal formatting.
86				raw, _ := json.Marshal(v)
87				crdtOp.Value = raw
88			case store.CRDTTypeGSet:
89				if len(op.Elements) == 0 {
90					writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each gset op must add at least one element")
91					return
92				}
93				for _, element := range op.Elements {
94					if element == "" {
95						writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "gset elements must be non-empty strings")
96						return
97					}
98				}
99				crdtOp.Elements = op.Elements
100			case store.CRDTTypeRegister:
101				// The value may be any JSON, null included; only an absent field
102				// (a nil RawMessage — an explicit null decodes to the bytes
103				// "null") is a missing field. The value is stored verbatim.
104				if op.Value == nil {
105					writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each register op must carry a value")
106					return
107				}
108				v, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(op.Version)
109				if !ok {
110					writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each register op must carry an integer version >= 0")
111					return
112				}
113				crdtOp.Value = op.Value
114				crdtOp.Version = v
115			}
116			ops[i] = crdtOp
117		}
118	
119		results, err := s.SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, req.Type, ops)
120		if err != nil {
121			var conflict *store.ErrCRDTConflict
122			switch {
123			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
124				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
125			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
126				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
127			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
128				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, conflict.Error())
129			default:
130				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit crdt ops")
131			}
132			return
133		}
134	
135		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
136	}

138	// handleCRDTState returns the document's current type and merged result. A
139	// document with no committed operations has no state yet and answers 404.
140	func handleCRDTState(s *store.Store, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
141		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
142	
143		state, err := s.GetCRDTState(documentID)
144		if err != nil {
145			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrCRDTNotFound) {
146				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "crdt state not found")
147				return
148			}
149			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to load crdt state")
150			return
151		}
152	
153		writeCRDTState(w, state)
154	}
155	
156	// handleSessionCRDTState is the session-scoped view of the document-level
157	// state read:
158	//
159	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
160	//
161	// The read identity is entirely the existing session (no new auth): the
162	// session's owning device is the credential and the validation order matches
163	// the other session-scoped reads exactly — request shape (400, enforced by the
164	// route and path guard before this handler), then session existence
165	// (404 JSON for a session that never existed or was deleted), then the
166	// session device's permission for the document (403 JSON with no state
167	// content), and finally the document's CRDT state. A document without any
168	// committed CRDT operation is the same 404 JSON as the document-level read, so
169	// a deleted session, an unknown document-state and a revoked permission remain
170	// three independent answers.
171	//
172	// On success the body is byte-for-byte the document-level state read's body
173	// (writeCRDTState): compact single-line JSON, keys type then value, one
174	// trailing newline. The endpoint is read-only: it renders the state derived by
175	// the store without advancing a cursor, writing a change, registering a
176	// subscription or affecting CRDT type fixation, idempotency or persistence; a
177	// restart changes neither the answer nor the status codes.
178	func handleSessionCRDTState(s *store.Store, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
179		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
180		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
181	
182		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
183		if err != nil {
184			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
185				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
186				return
187			}
188			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
189			return
190		}
191	
192		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
193		if err != nil {
194			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
195			return
196		}
197		if !authorized {
198			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
199			return
200		}
201	
202		state, err := s.GetCRDTState(documentID)
203		if err != nil {
204			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrCRDTNotFound) {
205				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "crdt state not found")
206				return
207			}
208			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to load crdt state")
209			return
210		}
211	
212		writeCRDTState(w, state)
213	}
214	
215	// writeCRDTState renders a CRDT state exactly as every state reader must:
216	// compact single-line JSON with the keys in type, value order, terminated by a
217	// newline (the json.Encoder output), shared by the document-level read, the
218	// session-scoped read and — via marshalCRDTState — the subscription push
219	// frames, so the three can be compared byte-for-byte.
220	func writeCRDTState(w http.ResponseWriter, state store.CRDTState) {
221		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
222		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
223		_, _ = w.Write(marshalCRDTState(state))
224	}
225	
226	// marshalCRDTState encodes a CRDT state the single way every surface emits it:
227	// compact single-line JSON with the keys in type, value order and one trailing
228	// newline. The value is embedded as native JSON (a number, an array, or a
229	// register's arbitrary JSON value) rather than an escaped blob.
230	func marshalCRDTState(state store.CRDTState) []byte {
231		var buf strings.Builder
232		enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
233		_ = enc.Encode(map[string]any{
234			"type":  state.Type,
235			"value": json.RawMessage(state.Value),
236		})
237		return []byte(buf.String())
238	}
239	
240	// malformedCRDTPath reports whether p targets the CRDT namespace but is not at
241	// one of the two exact endpoints:
242	//
243	//	POST/GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/crdt/ops
244	//	GET      /v1/documents/{documentID}/crdt/state
245	//
246	// A missing/empty document id, a trailing slash, extra path segments, or a
247	// "crdt" segment in any position short of that shape is a malformed 400 rather
248	// than ServeMux's redirect or plain-text 404/405, so the new endpoints never
249	// redirect or emit HTML. The keyword is matched only past the documentID
250	// position, so a document literally named "crdt" keeps its ordinary routes.
251	func malformedCRDTPath(p string) bool {
252		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
253		if !ok {
254			return false
255		}
256		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
257		for i, seg := range segs {
258			if seg == "crdt" && i > 0 {
259				if len(segs) != 3 || segs[0] == "" {
260					return true
261				}
262				switch segs[2] {
263				case "ops", "state":
264					return false
265				default:
266					return true
267				}
268			}
269		}
270		return false
271	}

1	// Package store persists document change batches in a SQLite database.
2	//
3	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
4	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
5	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
6	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically, so cursors never repeat and no
7	// record is partially written, even under concurrent writers.
8	//
9	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
10	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
11	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
12	// change log.
13	//
14	// A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a snapshot's state.
15	// Restore provenance (the snapshot cursor the state came from) is persisted in
16	// its own table, so after restart a repeated restore is still distinguishable
17	// from an ordinary change and idempotency/conflict decisions are unchanged.
18	//
19	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer on top of which clients
20	// sync. A device registers with a client-supplied id; a session belongs to
21	// exactly one registered device and is addressed by its own client-supplied
22	// id. Registration and session creation are idempotent re-posts: the first
23	// call creates, an identical repeat does not. A session id already owned by
24	// another device is a conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are
25	// owner-scoped and hard: a repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device
26	// path all miss with 404, after which the id is free to be created again.
27	//
28	// Document permissions sit on top of registration: every (document, device)
29	// pair starts authorized, and a grant or revoke is recorded per pair. Writes
30	// are serialized in one transaction and committed to disk, so concurrent
31	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
32	// Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots or sessions; it only gates the
33	// session-scoped change listing.
34	//
35	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
36	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
37	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
38	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
39	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
40	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
41	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
42	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
43	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them.
44	//
45	// Long polling lets a caught-up client wait for subsequent changes. Waiters
46	// register per document before the confirming read, so a commit landing
47	// between that read and the park is never missed; every change-producing
48	// commit (batch, merge, restore, replay) signals the document's waiters after
49	// it commits. Wait state is in-memory only — a canceled disconnect or a
50	// closing store leaves no rows behind — while the changes themselves stay
51	// durable, so waiting and idempotency decisions are unchanged by restart.
52	//
53	// Replay is the offline retry of an ordinary batch: it shares the same
54	// per-document contiguous cursor space and the same serialized transaction as
55	// PostChanges, and additionally enforces the registration/permission layer
56	// (ErrDeviceNotFound, ErrPermissionDenied) before any change id is resolved,
57	// so its error responses never reveal change content.
58	package store
59	
60	import (
61		"context"
62		"database/sql"
63		"encoding/json"
64		"errors"
65		"fmt"
66		"sync"
67		"time"
68	
69		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
70	)
71	
72	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the store is shutting down and parked long
73	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
74	// caller maps it to 503.
75	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
76	
77	// ErrPermissionDenied reports that a device's access to the document has been
78	// revoked. The caller maps it to 403; nothing is written and no change content
79	// is exposed.

187	// Store is the durable change log.
188	type Store struct {
189		db *sql.DB
190	
191		// pollMu guards pollWaits, subs, crdtSubs, nextWaitID, nextSubID,
192		// nextCRDTSubID and closed. Parked long polls wait on a per-document set
193		// of channels; a committed change to a document closes (signals) every
194		// channel parked on it. WebSocket subscriptions live in a second registry
195		// keyed by (document, device): a commit signals every subscription under
196		// the document, while a permission write signals only the matching
197		// device's subscriptions. CRDT state subscriptions live in a third
198		// registry with the same keying: a state-changing CRDT commit queues the
199		// new merged state on every subscription under the document.
200		pollMu        sync.Mutex
201		pollWaits     map[string]map[uint64]chan struct{}
202		subs          map[subKey]map[uint64]*subscription
203		crdtSubs      map[crdtSubKey]map[uint64]*CRDTSubscription
204		nextWaitID    uint64
205		nextSubID     uint64
206		nextCRDTSubID uint64
207		subWG         sync.WaitGroup
208		closed        bool
209	
210		// crdtMu serializes CRDT submissions against each other and against a
211		// subscription's atomic register-plus-initial-read. Holding it across a
212		// state-changing commit and its notification makes notifications leave in
213		// transaction-commit order, and makes a commit's state land either in a
214		// subscriber's initial read or in its queue, never both and never
215		// neither. The single database connection already serializes the
216		// transactions themselves, so this costs no concurrency.
217		crdtMu sync.Mutex
218	}

220	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
221	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
222	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
223		if path == "" {
224			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
225			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
226			path = "file::memory:"
227		}
228		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
229		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
230		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
231		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
232		if err != nil {
233			return nil, err
234		}
235		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
236		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
237		// for readers does not help correctness here.
238		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
239		s := &Store{
240			db:        db,
241			pollWaits: make(map[string]map[uint64]chan struct{}),
242			subs:      make(map[subKey]map[uint64]*subscription),
243			crdtSubs:  make(map[crdtSubKey]map[uint64]*CRDTSubscription),
244		}
245		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
246			_ = db.Close()
247			return nil, err
248		}
249		return s, nil
250	}

320	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll without closing the database,
321	// so an orderly server shutdown drains waiting connections immediately
322	// (they answer 503) instead of holding Shutdown hostage until their wait
323	// deadline. Committed state is untouched.
324	func (s *Store) InterruptWaits() {
325		s.pollMu.Lock()
326		s.closed = true
327		waits := s.pollWaits
328		s.pollWaits = map[string]map[uint64]chan struct{}{}
329		// Snapshot the live subscription channels without reaping the registry:
330		// unregister remains valid while handlers drain, so the WaitGroup in
331		// Close balances. New AddSubscription calls fail fast on closed.
332		var subChans []chan struct{}
333		for _, set := range s.subs {
334			for _, sub := range set {
335				subChans = append(subChans, sub.wakes)
336			}
337		}
338		s.pollMu.Unlock()
339		for _, set := range waits {
340			for _, ch := range set {
341				close(ch)
342			}
343		}
344		// Live subscriptions get one last wakeup as well; the server re-checks
345		// the closed flag and finishes the connection with a going-away close.
346		for _, ch := range subChans {
347			select {
348			case ch <- struct{}{}:
349			default:
350			}
351		}
352		// CRDT state subscriptions get the same final wakeup.
353		s.wakeCRDTSubscribers()
354	}
355	
356	// Close releases the database handle. Parked long polls are woken first so
357	// they stop waiting and return without writing; the wake happens before the
358	// handle closes, so a waiter never observes a closed database. WebSocket
359	// subscriptions (change-log and CRDT state alike) are likewise woken and
360	// drained (every handler unregisters) before the handle closes.
361	func (s *Store) Close() error {
362		s.InterruptWaits()
363		s.subWG.Wait()
364		return s.db.Close()
365	}

367	// registerWait parks a channel for documentID and returns it together with a
368	// removal function. The channel is closed on the next committed change to the
369	// document, or when the store closes.
370	func (s *Store) registerWait(documentID string) (ch chan struct{}, remove func()) {
371		ch = make(chan struct{}, 1)
372	
373		s.pollMu.Lock()
374		defer s.pollMu.Unlock()
375		if s.closed {
376			// Close beat the registration: signal immediately so the caller does
377			// not park on a channel nobody will close.
378			close(ch)
379			return ch, func() {}
380		}
381		s.nextWaitID++
382		id := s.nextWaitID
383		set := s.pollWaits[documentID]
384		if set == nil {
385			set = make(map[uint64]chan struct{})
386			s.pollWaits[documentID] = set
387		}
388		set[id] = ch
389		return ch, func() {
390			s.pollMu.Lock()
391			if set, ok := s.pollWaits[documentID]; ok {
392				delete(set, id)
393				if len(set) == 0 {
394					delete(s.pollWaits, documentID)
395				}
396			}
397			s.pollMu.Unlock()
398		}
399	}
400	
401	// notifyWaiters signals every long poll parked on documentID and every
402	// WebSocket subscription open on it. It is called only after a
403	// change-bearing transaction has committed, so parked readers observe the
404	// new rows when they re-query and pushed frames describe committed changes.
405	func (s *Store) notifyWaiters(documentID string) {
406		s.pollMu.Lock()
407		set := s.pollWaits[documentID]
408		delete(s.pollWaits, documentID)
409		s.pollMu.Unlock()
410		for _, ch := range set {
411			close(ch)
412		}
413		s.signalSubscribers(documentID)
414	}
415	
416	// WaitForChanges blocks until documentID has a change with cursor greater than
417	// after, a change is committed while waiting, wait elapses, ctx is canceled
418	// (the client disconnected) or the store closes. It then returns the current
419	// page of up to limit changes exactly as ListChanges would, with timedOut=true
420	// only when the wait deadline expired with no new rows.
421	//
422	// Registration precedes the first query: a commit landing between the read and
423	// the park still notifies a registered channel, so no change is missed.
424	//
425	// An unknown document is never parked on: it returns immediately with an empty
426	// list and nextCursor 0, timedOut=false. Data already past after is likewise
427	// returned immediately. wait <= 0 is an immediately expired deadline.
428	func (s *Store) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) (changes []ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool, err error) {
429		ch, remove := s.registerWait(documentID)
430		defer remove()
431	
432		changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
433		if err != nil || len(changes) > 0 {
434			return changes, nextCursor, false, err
435		}
436	
437		// Empty page: distinguish an unknown document (immediate empty/0, never
438		// parked on) from a known document caught up to after.
439		known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
440		if err != nil || !known {
441			return changes, 0, false, err
442		}
443	
444		// Known document, nothing new: a zero wait is an immediately expired
445		// deadline; ListChanges already echoes nextCursor == after.
446		if wait <= 0 {
447			return changes, nextCursor, true, nil
448		}
449	
450		timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
451		defer timer.Stop()
452	
453		select {
454		case <-ch:
455			// Woken by a committed change or by Close.
456			s.pollMu.Lock()
457			closing := s.closed
458			s.pollMu.Unlock()
459			if closing {
460				return nil, 0, false, ErrStoreClosing
461			}
462			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
463			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
464		case <-timer.C:
465			// Timeout with no new rows: echo the caller's cursor without
466			// advancing it. The document was known above, so ListChanges returns
467			// nextCursor == after for an empty page.
468			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
469			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
470		case <-ctx.Done():
471			return nil, 0, false, ctx.Err()
472		}
473	}

475	// DocumentExists reports whether documentID has any change row and is
476	// therefore a known document rather than an empty namespace.
477	func (s *Store) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
478		var known bool
479		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
480			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)`,
481			documentID,
482		).Scan(&known); err != nil {
483			return false, err
484		}
485		return known, nil
486	}

488	// PostChanges validates and commits one batch atomically.
489	//
490	// Every change must have a non-empty id; duplicate ids within the batch are
491	// rejected by the caller before reaching this point. On conflict the returned
492	// error is *ErrConflict and nothing is written. Cursors are assigned in batch
493	// order to ids that do not yet exist. Results are returned in the same order
494	// as the input.
495	func (s *Store) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []Change) ([]Result, error) {
496		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
497		if err != nil {
498			return nil, err
499		}
500		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
501	
502		results := make([]Result, len(changes))
503	
504		// First pass: resolve every id against existing rows. A single mismatch
505		// aborts the whole batch before any cursor is allocated.
506		pending := make([]int, 0, len(changes))
507		for i, c := range changes {
508			var existingDevice string
509			var existingPayload []byte
510			var existingCursor int64
511			err := tx.QueryRow(
512				`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
513				documentID, c.ID,
514			).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
515			switch {
516			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
517				pending = append(pending, i)
518			case err != nil:
519				return nil, err
520			default:
521				if existingDevice != c.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingPayload, c.Payload) {
522					return nil, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
523				}
524				results[i] = Result{
525					ID:      c.ID,
526					Created: false,
527					Cursor:  existingCursor,
528				}
529			}
530		}
531	
532		// Allocate cursors for genuinely new ids.
533		var nextCursor int64
534		if err := tx.QueryRow(
535			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
536			documentID,
537		).Scan(&nextCursor); err != nil {
538			return nil, err
539		}
540		for _, i := range pending {
541			c := changes[i]
542			if _, err := tx.Exec(
543				`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
544				documentID, nextCursor, c.ID, c.DeviceID, []byte(c.Payload),
545			); err != nil {
546				return nil, err
547			}
548			results[i] = Result{
549				ID:      c.ID,
550				Created: true,
551				Cursor:  nextCursor,
552			}
553			nextCursor++
554		}
555	
556		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
557			return nil, err
558		}
559		if len(pending) > 0 {
560			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
561		}
562		return results, nil
563	}

565	// ReplayChanges commits a retried offline batch with exactly the same change
566	// semantics as PostChanges: ids resolve against the existing log, matching ids
567	// are idempotent only when deviceID and the decoded payload match, a mismatch
568	// is *ErrConflict and aborts the whole batch, and new ids take contiguous
569	// cursors in input order in one serialized transaction.
570	//
571	// Unlike PostChanges it additionally enforces the registration/permission
572	// layer before touching the log: an unregistered device yields
573	// ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and a revoked device yields ErrPermissionDenied
574	// (403). None of those outcomes writes anything or exposes change content.
575	func (s *Store) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []Change) ([]Result, error) {
576		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
577		if err != nil {
578			return nil, err
579		}
580		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
581	
582		// Gate first, in the same transaction: the device row and the permission
583		// row are read before any change id is resolved, so a rejected replay
584		// cannot observe (and its error cannot reveal) change content.
585		var deviceExists bool
586		if err := tx.QueryRow(
587			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, changes[0].DeviceID,
588		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
589			return nil, err
590		}
591		if !deviceExists {
592			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
593		}
594		var stored int
595		err = tx.QueryRow(
596			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
597			documentID, changes[0].DeviceID,
598		).Scan(&stored)
599		switch {
600		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
601			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
602		case err != nil:
603			return nil, err
604		default:
605			if stored == 0 {
606				return nil, ErrPermissionDenied
607			}
608		}
609	
610		results := make([]Result, len(changes))
611	
612		// Resolve every id before allocating anything.
613		pending := make([]int, 0, len(changes))
614		for i, c := range changes {
615			var existingDevice string
616			var existingPayload []byte
617			var existingCursor int64
618			err := tx.QueryRow(
619				`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
620				documentID, c.ID,
621			).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
622			switch {
623			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
624				pending = append(pending, i)
625			case err != nil:
626				return nil, err
627			default:
628				if existingDevice != c.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingPayload, c.Payload) {
629					return nil, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
630				}
631				results[i] = Result{
632					ID:      c.ID,
633					Created: false,
634					Cursor:  existingCursor,
635				}
636			}
637		}
638	
639		var nextCursor int64
640		if err := tx.QueryRow(
641			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
642			documentID,
643		).Scan(&nextCursor); err != nil {
644			return nil, err
645		}
646		for _, i := range pending {
647			c := changes[i]
648			if _, err := tx.Exec(
649				`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
650				documentID, nextCursor, c.ID, c.DeviceID, []byte(c.Payload),
651			); err != nil {
652				return nil, err
653			}
654			results[i] = Result{
655				ID:      c.ID,
656				Created: true,
657				Cursor:  nextCursor,
658			}
659			nextCursor++
660		}
661	
662		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
663			return nil, err
664		}
665		if len(pending) > 0 {
666			s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
667		}
668		return results, nil
669	}

671	// MergeChange validates and appends one change against a caller-observed base
672	// cursor, all within a single serialized transaction.
673	//
674	//   - An existing id is idempotent only when deviceId and the decoded payload
675	//     match (Outcome "idempotent", with the original Result); a mismatch is an
676	//     *ErrConflict and nothing is written.
677	//   - A new id with baseCursor equal to the current cursor is appended as
678	//     "applied".
679	//   - A new id with a base cursor behind the current one is appended as
680	//     "merged" only when every change after baseCursor carries a JSON object
681	//     payload whose top-level keys are disjoint from the new payload's; any
682	//     non-object later payload or shared key is an *ErrConflict.
683	//
684	// A non-zero baseCursor for an unknown document, or a baseCursor greater than
685	// the current cursor, returns ErrStaleCursor. An unknown document with
686	// baseCursor 0 accepts the first change as "applied".
687	func (s *Store) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c Change) (MergeResult, error) {
688		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
689		if err != nil {
690			return MergeResult{}, err
691		}
692		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
693	
694		// Current cursor is the document's high-water mark, 0 when unknown.
695		var current int64
696		if err := tx.QueryRow(
697			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
698			documentID,
699		).Scan(&current); err != nil {
700			return MergeResult{}, err
701		}
702		if baseCursor > current || (baseCursor != 0 && current == 0) {
703			return MergeResult{}, ErrStaleCursor
704		}
705	
706		// An existing id keeps the original idempotency/conflict rules.
707		var existingDevice string
708		var existingPayload []byte
709		var existingCursor int64
710		err = tx.QueryRow(
711			`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
712			documentID, c.ID,
713		).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
714		switch {
715		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
716			// New id; fall through to append logic below.
717		case err != nil:
718			return MergeResult{}, err
719		default:
720			if existingDevice != c.DeviceID || !jsonEqual(existingPayload, c.Payload) {
721				return MergeResult{}, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
722			}
723			return MergeResult{
724				ID:      c.ID,
725				Outcome: "idempotent",
726				Cursor:  existingCursor,
727				Result: &Result{
728					ID:      c.ID,
729					Created: false,
730					Cursor:  existingCursor,
731				},
732			}, nil
733		}
734	
735		outcome := "applied"
736		if baseCursor < current {
737			// Merge is allowed only when every change after baseCursor is a JSON
738			// object whose top-level keys do not collide with the new payload's.
739			newKeys, err := objectKeys(c.Payload)
740			if err != nil {
741				if errors.Is(err, errNotObject) {
742					return MergeResult{}, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
743				}
744				return MergeResult{}, err
745			}
746			rows, err := tx.Query(
747				`SELECT payload FROM changes
748				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor > ?
749				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
750				documentID, baseCursor,
751			)
752			if err != nil {
753				return MergeResult{}, err
754			}
755			for rows.Next() {
756				var laterPayload []byte
757				if err := rows.Scan(&laterPayload); err != nil {
758					_ = rows.Close()
759					return MergeResult{}, err
760				}
761				laterKeys, err := objectKeys(laterPayload)
762				if err != nil {
763					_ = rows.Close()
764					if errors.Is(err, errNotObject) {
765						return MergeResult{}, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
766					}
767					return MergeResult{}, err
768				}
769				for k := range newKeys {
770					if _, clash := laterKeys[k]; clash {
771						_ = rows.Close()
772						return MergeResult{}, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
773					}
774				}
775			}
776			if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
777				_ = rows.Close()
778				return MergeResult{}, err
779			}
780			_ = rows.Close()
781			outcome = "merged"
782		}
783	
784		next := current + 1
785		if _, err := tx.Exec(
786			`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
787			documentID, next, c.ID, c.DeviceID, []byte(c.Payload),
788		); err != nil {
789			return MergeResult{}, err
790		}
791	
792		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
793			return MergeResult{}, err
794		}
795		s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
796		return MergeResult{ID: c.ID, Outcome: outcome, Cursor: next}, nil
797	}

799	// PutSnapshot stores state as the snapshot of documentID at cursor, creating
800	// it on first use and reporting whether this call created it.
801	//
802	// Only cursors of existing changes are valid snapshot points: an unknown
803	// document, a cursor below 1 or a cursor ahead of the document's current
804	// cursor yields ErrSnapshotBase and nothing is written. Re-posting a state
805	// that decodes equal to the stored one is idempotent (created=false); a
806	// different state is an *ErrSnapshotConflict and the stored snapshot is left
807	// unchanged. Snapshots are independent of the change log: they neither move
808	// the document's cursor nor affect merges.
809	func (s *Store) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
810		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
811		if err != nil {
812			return false, err
813		}
814		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
815	
816		var current int64
817		if err := tx.QueryRow(
818			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
819			documentID,
820		).Scan(&current); err != nil {
821			return false, err
822		}
823		if current == 0 || cursor < 1 || cursor > current {
824			return false, ErrSnapshotBase
825		}
826	
827		var existing []byte
828		err = tx.QueryRow(
829			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
830			documentID, cursor,
831		).Scan(&existing)
832		switch {
833		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
834			if _, err := tx.Exec(
835				`INSERT INTO snapshots (document_id, cursor, state) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
836				documentID, cursor, []byte(state),
837			); err != nil {
838				return false, err
839			}
840			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
841				return false, err
842			}
843			return true, nil
844		case err != nil:
845			return false, err
846		default:
847			if !jsonEqual(existing, state) {
848				return false, &ErrSnapshotConflict{Cursor: cursor}
849			}
850			return false, nil
851		}
852	}

873	// RestoreSnapshot appends one ordinary change whose payload is the state of
874	// documentID's snapshot at snapshotCursor, all within a single serialized
875	// transaction.
876	//
877	//   - A snapshot miss (unknown document or a cursor without a snapshot)
878	//     returns ErrSnapshotNotFound; nothing is written.
879	//   - If changeID already belongs to a prior restore, the call is idempotent
880	//     only when deviceId, snapshotCursor and the decoded source state all
881	//     match; the first result (created=false, original cursor) is returned.
882	//   - If changeID is taken by an ordinary change, or a restore whose provenance
883	//     differs, the call returns *ErrRestoreConflict; nothing is written.
884	//
885	// Otherwise a new change is appended with the next document cursor and the
886	// restore provenance is recorded. Old rows are never modified.
887	func (s *Store) RestoreSnapshot(documentID string, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (RestoreResult, error) {
888		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
889		if err != nil {
890			return RestoreResult{}, err
891		}
892		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
893	
894		// The snapshot must exist; its state is the payload to append.
895		var state []byte
896		err = tx.QueryRow(
897			`SELECT state FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor = ?`,
898			documentID, snapshotCursor,
899		).Scan(&state)
900		switch {
901		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
902			return RestoreResult{}, ErrSnapshotNotFound
903		case err != nil:
904			return RestoreResult{}, err
905		}
906	
907		// Resolve the change id: an ordinary row and a prior restore are handled
908		// differently, so consult both tables.
909		var existingCursor int64
910		var existingDevice string
911		var existingPayload []byte
912		err = tx.QueryRow(
913			`SELECT cursor, device_id, payload FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
914			documentID, changeID,
915		).Scan(&existingCursor, &existingDevice, &existingPayload)
916		switch {
917		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
918			// New id; fall through to append below.
919		case err != nil:
920			return RestoreResult{}, err
921		default:
922			var restDevice string
923			var restSnapshotCursor int64
924			var restState []byte
925			err = tx.QueryRow(
926				`SELECT device_id, snapshot_cursor, state FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
927				documentID, changeID,
928			).Scan(&restDevice, &restSnapshotCursor, &restState)
929			switch {
930			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
931				// The id belongs to an ordinary change (or a batch/merge change),
932				// not a restore: never treat it as an idempotent restore.
933				return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
934			case err != nil:
935				return RestoreResult{}, err
936			default:
937				if restDevice != deviceID || restSnapshotCursor != snapshotCursor || !jsonEqual(restState, state) {
938					return RestoreResult{}, &ErrRestoreConflict{ID: changeID}
939				}
940				return RestoreResult{
941					ID:           changeID,
942					Created:      false,
943					Cursor:       existingCursor,
944					RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
945				}, nil
946			}
947		}
948	
949		var nextCursor int64
950		if err := tx.QueryRow(
951			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
952			documentID,
953		).Scan(&nextCursor); err != nil {
954			return RestoreResult{}, err
955		}
956		if _, err := tx.Exec(
957			`INSERT INTO changes (document_id, cursor, id, device_id, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
958			documentID, nextCursor, changeID, deviceID, state,
959		); err != nil {
960			return RestoreResult{}, err
961		}
962		if _, err := tx.Exec(
963			`INSERT INTO restores (document_id, change_id, device_id, snapshot_cursor, change_cursor, state)
964			 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
965			documentID, changeID, deviceID, snapshotCursor, nextCursor, state,
966		); err != nil {
967			return RestoreResult{}, err
968		}
969	
970		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
971			return RestoreResult{}, err
972		}
973		s.notifyWaiters(documentID)
974		return RestoreResult{
975			ID:           changeID,
976			Created:      true,
977			Cursor:       nextCursor,
978			RestoredFrom: snapshotCursor,
979		}, nil
980	}

982	// RegisterDevice registers a device by client-supplied id. The first call for
983	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
984	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.
985	func (s *Store) RegisterDevice(deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
986		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
987		if err != nil {
988			return false, err
989		}
990		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
991	
992		var exists bool
993		if err := tx.QueryRow(
994			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
995		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
996			return false, err
997		}
998		if !exists {
999			if _, err := tx.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
1000				return false, err
1001			}
1002			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
1003				return false, err
1004			}
1005			return true, nil
1006		}
1007		// An idempotent repeat commits nothing; releasing the read transaction is
1008		// enough.
1009		return false, tx.Commit()
1010	}

1020	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
1021	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
1022	// cannot both create it.

1024		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
1025		if err != nil {
1026			return false, err

1028		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
1029	
1030		var deviceExists bool
1031		if err := tx.QueryRow(
1032			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
1033		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
1034			return false, err
1035		}
1036		if !deviceExists {
1037			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
1038		}
1039	
1040		var owner string
1041		err = tx.QueryRow(
1042			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
1043		).Scan(&owner)
1044		switch {
1045		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
1046			if _, err := tx.Exec(
1047				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
1048				sessionID, deviceID,
1049			); err != nil {
1050				return false, err
1051			}
1052			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
1053				return false, err
1054			}
1055			return true, nil
1056		case err != nil:
1057			return false, err
1058		}
1059	
1060		if owner != deviceID {
1061			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}

1133	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
1134	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
1135	//
1136	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
1137	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
1138	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
1139	// yields ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the write
1140	// run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls each
1141	// commit completely and the final state matches the last committed action.
1142	func (s *Store) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
1143		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
1144		if err != nil {
1145			return false, err
1146		}
1147		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
1148	
1149		var deviceExists bool
1150		if err := tx.QueryRow(
1151			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
1152		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
1153			return false, err
1154		}
1155		if !deviceExists {
1156			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
1157		}
1158	
1159		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
1160		var stored int
1161		err = tx.QueryRow(
1162			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
1163			documentID, deviceID,
1164		).Scan(&stored)
1165		switch {
1166		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
1167			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
1168		case err != nil:
1169			return false, err
1170		default:
1171			current = stored != 0
1172		}
1173		if current == authorized {
1174			return false, tx.Commit()
1175		}
1176	
1177		v := 0
1178		if authorized {
1179			v = 1
1180		}
1181		if _, err := tx.Exec(
1182			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
1183			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
1184			documentID, deviceID, v,
1185		); err != nil {
1186			return false, err
1187		}
1188		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
1189			return false, err
1190		}
1191		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
1192		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
1193		if !authorized {
1194			s.signalRevokedSubscribers(documentID, deviceID)
1195			s.signalRevokedCRDTSubscribers(documentID, deviceID)
1196		}
1197		return true, nil
1198	}

1221	// objectKeys returns the top-level keys of a JSON object payload. A null,
1222	// array or scalar payload yields errNotObject.
1223	func objectKeys(raw json.RawMessage) (map[string]struct{}, error) {
1224		var m map[string]json.RawMessage
1225		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
1226			// Valid JSON that is not an object (array, scalar, null) decodes with
1227			// a type error into a map; treat it and malformed JSON as non-object.
1228			return nil, errNotObject
1229		}
1230		if m == nil {
1231			return nil, errNotObject
1232		}
1233		keys := make(map[string]struct{}, len(m))
1234		for k := range m {
1235			keys[k] = struct{}{}
1236		}
1237		return keys, nil
1238	}
